| `domain` | body | string | no | Bare hostname e.g. "example.com". Empty string clears. |
| `language` | body | string | no | Default content language as a BCP-47 tag (e.g. "en", "sv", "en-GB"). Drives &lt;html lang&gt; and the default for alt-text generation. Empty string clears. |
| `ai_scripts_enabled` | body | boolean | no | "Allow AI to write block scripts": lets the in-portal chat assistant author block JavaScript for this site. API keys and MCP are not gated by it — they can always write block `script` and core/embed `js`. Requires admin permission. |

## Site: Domain

### `read_domain`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/domain`

Permission: `read`

Read the current state of the site's custom domain. Returns `{ hostname, status, dns_target, verified_at, failure_reason }` or `null` when no domain is attached. Status is one of 'pending' (DNS not yet verified), 'verified' (DNS + cert OK, awaiting customer activation), 'live' (production URL is now the custom domain), 'failed' (Cloudflare returned an error — see failure_reason).

### `add_domain`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/domain`

Permission: `write`

Attach a custom domain to this site. The site MUST NOT already have a domain set — remove the existing one first. Declaring the domain makes it canonical immediately and queues a production deploy by default; point DNS only after that deploy. Returns the CNAME target. Use `poll_domain` to observe DNS/SSL verification. There is no separate activation step in the current domain-first workflow.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `hostname` | body | string | yes | Hostname to attach, e.g. "www.example.com". Leading https:// and trailing slashes are stripped. |
| `prefer` | body | "apex" \| "www" | no | Canonical host for an apex/www pair. Defaults to apex. |
| `auto_deploy` | body | boolean | no | Default true. Publish the canonical/sitemap change before DNS cutover. |

### `poll_domain`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/domain/poll`

Permission: `write`

Ask Cloudflare for the current state of the attached domain and update the site doc accordingly. Idempotent — call after DNS changes propagate. Returns the new state; status may have advanced from 'pending' to 'verified' or 'failed'.

### `activate_domain`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/domain/activate`

Permission: `write`

Legacy compatibility tool; new workflows should not call it. A declared domain is already canonical and becomes visitable when DNS verifies. For legacy records only, this changes the stored verified state to live. Precondition: status must be 'verified' (or already 'live' — idempotent). By default it also enqueues a production deploy; the response includes `deploy.job_id` you can poll. Pass `auto_deploy: false` to skip that compatibility deploy.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `auto_deploy` | body | boolean | no | Default true. Enqueue a production deploy after activation so canonical URLs update. |

### `remove_domain`

`DELETE /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/domain`

Permission: `write`

Detach the custom domain from this site and clear it from the site doc. Use this when the customer wants to start over with a different hostname or move the site to a different domain provider.

## Site: Extensions

### `call_extension_admin`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/extensions/{installation_id}/admin-request`

Permission: `write`

Call an enabled app’s approved admin API using the current site administrator identity. Read that installed app’s guide first for supported paths and effects. GET reads; POST can change app settings. No deployment is queued by Core. Ordinary admin credentials only; installation credentials cannot delegate. Tokens stay server-side.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `installation_id` | path | string | yes |  |
| `page_id` | body | string | yes |  |
| `path` | body | string | yes | Relative operation below the approved native API base, from the installed app guide. |
| `method` | body | "GET" \| "POST" | yes |  |
| `query` | body | object | no |  |
| `body` | body | object | no |  |

### `list_extension_installations`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/extensions`

Permission: `admin`

List the site's installed Extensions, including installation ids, manifests, config schemas, and masked current config. Read this before updating installation config. Admin permission required.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | query | string | no | Branch id to target. Omit for main. An id that does not name a version of this Site is refused with 404 — it is never answered about main instead. |

### `read_extension_installation`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/extensions/{installation_id}`

Permission: `admin`

Read one Extension installation, its manifest config schema, and its masked current config. Secret values are never returned. Admin permission required.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | query | string | no | Branch id to target. Omit for main. An id that does not name a version of this Site is refused with 404 — it is never answered about main instead. |
| `installation_id` | path | string | yes | Installation id returned by list_extension_installations. |

### `activate_extension_release`

`PATCH /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/extensions/{installation_id}`

Permission: `admin`

Explicitly activate a pending migration release for this site only. First read_extension_installation and review pending_activation_manifest, configuration and app migration instructions. Changes runtime selection immediately; never queues publication. Existing permissions remain unless granted_scopes is explicitly supplied. Admin permission required.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `installation_id` | path | string | yes |  |
| `version` | body | string | yes | Pending published release to activate. |
| `config` | body | object | no |  |
| `granted_scopes` | body | string[] | no |  |

### `update_extension_installation_config`

`PATCH /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/extensions/{installation_id}`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/deploy`

Permission: `admin`

Update schema-defined config for an installed Extension. Call read_extension_installation first and send only keys declared by manifest.config_schema. Omitted fields preserve their current values, including masked secrets. This can update public content such as consent text, policy-link text, and policy URLs. Public fields are versioned; private configuration and credentials can only change on main. A deploy of the selected version is queued by default (main: production, other versions: staging); pass deploy:false only when batching changes and deploy later. Admin permission required.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | query | string | no | Branch id to target. Omit for main. An id that does not name a version of this Site is refused with 404 — it is never answered about main instead. |
| `installation_id` | path | string | yes | Installation id returned by list_extension_installations. |
| `config` | body | object | yes | Config keys and values declared by the installation manifest config schema. |
| `deploy` | body | boolean | no | Queue a deploy of the selected site version after saving. Defaults to true. |

### `install_extension`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/extensions`

Permission: `admin`

Install an Extension release on this site, as the portal's install action does. Pass the Extension id and a published release (developer organizations may also install their own draft or review releases on their own sites). granted_scopes must be a subset of the manifest's requested permissions — grant only what the user approved. config must satisfy manifest.config_schema; secret values are encrypted and never returned. Does not deploy: trigger_deploy afterwards to publish provisioned components. Admin permission required.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `extension_id` | body | string | yes |  |
| `version` | body | string | yes | Release version to install. |
| `granted_scopes` | body | string[] | no | Approved scopes; defaults to none. |
| `config` | body | object | no |  |
| `developer_org_id` | body | string | no | Organization that publishes the Extension. Defaults to the key's own organization. |

### `set_extension_installation_status`

`PATCH /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/extensions/{installation_id}`

Permission: `admin`

Enable or disable an installed Extension on this site. Disabling removes its components from the public snapshot and editor until re-enabled; page instances are kept. Changes apply immediately to previews; deploy to publish. Admin permission required.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `installation_id` | path | string | yes |  |
| `status` | body | "enabled" \| "disabled" | yes |  |

### `uninstall_extension`

`DELETE /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/extensions/{installation_id}`

Permission: `admin`

Uninstall an Extension from this site: revokes the installation and all its server credentials and removes its block definitions. Existing page blocks remain as unavailable placeholders. Not reversible except by installing again (a new installation id). Get explicit user approval. Admin permission required.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `installation_id` | path | string | yes |  |

### `pair_extension_issuer`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/extensions/{installation_id}/pair`

Permission: `admin`

Pair this Typeroll instance's token issuer with the Extension provider (manifest auth.pairing_url), the portal's "secure connection" action. Contacts the provider. Returns the trusted issuer record. Admin permission required.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `installation_id` | path | string | yes |  |

### `read_extension_diagnostics`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/extensions/{installation_id}/diagnostics`

Permission: `admin`

Read an installation's diagnostics: status, health, release resolution, credential metadata (no secrets), the latest audit events and lifecycle event deliveries, and declared URL context inputs. Admin permission required.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `installation_id` | path | string | yes |  |

### `launch_extension_admin_page`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/extensions/{installation_id}/launch`

Permission: `write`

Issue a single-use, short-lived launch grant for one of the Extension's admin pages (manifest admin.pages), as opening the page in the portal does. Returns { launch_url, method, form, expires_at }: a browser tool must POST the `form` fields to launch_url before expires_at. The provider sees the caller as api-key:{prefix}. Treat the code as a credential. For approved native pages prefer call_extension_admin. The page's minimum_permission applies.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `installation_id` | path | string | yes |  |
| `page_id` | body | string | yes | Admin page id from the installation manifest. |

## Site: Fonts

### `search_fonts`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/fonts/catalog`

Permission: `read`

Search the font catalog (250 open-licence Google Fonts families with their weights, italics, variable weight axis and extended Latin support) and the site's own families: uploaded files (`library`) and font services (`services`), matching the same query. Exact names rank first, then names starting with the query. Use it before set_site_fonts to check a family exists and has the weights the design needs. Swedish, Norwegian, Danish, Finnish and German are covered by every catalog family; latin_ext adds Polish, Czech, Turkish and more. Where a family loads from, in order: the site's Fonts library (uploaded files, upload_font), a font service in fonts.services (Adobe Fonts kit, Bunny Fonts or Fontshare stylesheet, loaded from their CDN), "system" (the device's own fonts, no download), and otherwise Google Fonts. Google families are self-hosted by default (fonts.delivery "self_hosted": the files are copied into the published site, no request to Google), or loaded from the Google Fonts CDN with delivery "google".

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | query | string | no | Part of a family name, e.g. "grotesk" or "Playfair". |
| `category` | query | "sans" \| "serif" \| "display" \| "handwriting" \| "mono" \| "sans" \| "serif" \| "display" \| "handwriting" \| "mono"[] | no |  |
| `variable` | query | boolean | no | Only variable families (one file covers every weight). |
| `italic` | query | boolean | no | Only families with italics. |
| `latin_ext` | query | boolean | no | Only families with the extended Latin subset. |
| `limit` | query | integer | no | Catalog results to return (default 50). |

### `upload_font`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/fonts`

Permission: `admin`

Add a font file to the site's Fonts library (not the media library), so a role can use its family with set_site_fonts. WOFF2, WOFF, TTF or OTF up to 10 MB, one font per file (no .ttc collections); anything but WOFF2 is converted to WOFF2 and the original kept. Family, weight and style default from the file; pass them to correct the file's names. A variable font covers a weight range ("100-900"). Upload one file per style (regular, italic) and, for static fonts, per weight. licence_confirmed must be true and means the user confirmed the font's licence allows use on this website (a webfont or web licence; most desktop licences do not include it). Ask the user before uploading; never assume it. It is stored with who confirmed it and when. Send the file as data_base64 with filename, or as source_url (https; downloaded by Typeroll). Requires admin permission. The library belongs to the site, not to a branch. Adobe Fonts cannot be uploaded (its licence does not allow self-hosting): add the kit with set_site_fonts services instead.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `filename` | body | string | no | The file name, e.g. "BrandSans-Regular.woff2". Required with data_base64. |
| `data_base64` | body | string | no | The file bytes, base64-encoded (a data: URL prefix is allowed). |
| `source_url` | body | string | no | An https:// URL to download the file from, instead of data_base64. |
| `family` | body | string | no | The family name the roles use. Defaults to the name in the file. |
| `weight` | body | integer \| string | no | 400, or a range such as "100-900" for a variable font. Defaults to the file's weight. |
| `style` | body | "normal" \| "italic" | no | Defaults to the file's style. |
| `category` | body | "sans" \| "serif" | no | Chooses the metric-matched fallback shown while the font loads (Arial or Times New Roman). Defaults to sans. |
| `licence_confirmed` | body | boolean | yes | true: the user confirmed the licence allows using this font on this website. |
| `licence_note` | body | string | no | Where the licence comes from, e.g. "Web licence, order 1234". |

## Site: Form capabilities

### `get_form_capabilities`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/form-capabilities`

Permission: `read`

List the action types a form can run after a submission (core "email" and "webhook" plus types provided by installed apps) and the prefill sources, each with its config field schema — the same choices as the portal's Forms editor. Read this before writing `actions` with create_form/update_form. Admin permission required.

## Site: Forms

### `list_forms`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/forms`

Permission: `read`

List every form defined on the site with its full field schema.

### `read_form`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/forms/{form_id}`

Permission: `read`

Read one form by id, including fields/steps, submit_text, success_message and, for admins, its actions (email notifications and webhooks; secrets masked). Place it with a `core/form` block using data.form_id on a block-mode page, or `<x-form id="…" />` in HTML mode. Both references are expanded server-side with validation, signed token, initial state, and the shared runtime.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `form_id` | path | string | yes |  |

### `create_form`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/forms`

Permission: `write`

Create a form. Steps are the ONLY stored model — a Block[] tree of form/* field blocks per step. Simple forms: pass `fields`, each { name, type, label, required?, placeholder?, options? } (allowed types: text, email, tel, url, number, textarea, select, checkbox, boolean (Yes/No/unanswered), radio, hidden, gdpr_consent) — the server converts them to a single static step; read_form returns the resulting steps. Multi-step funnels: pass `steps` directly (steps swap client-side, partial submissions persist per step; each step may set submit_label, and allow_back/show_progress control the Back button and progress indicator; `warnings` in the response flags steps whose title duplicates a leading form/heading). PLACING THE FORM: add a `core/form` block with data.form_id on block-mode pages, or `<x-form id="…" />` to HTML-mode page content. Both expand server-side to the same complete signed shell; never hand-write the form or add inline submit scripts.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | body | string | yes |  |
| `name` | body | string | yes |  |
| `fields` | body | object[] | no |  |
| `steps` | body | object[] | no |  |
| `submit_text` | body | string | no |  |
| `success_message` | body | string | no | Shown after the final step. May contain basic HTML (links, emphasis); it is sanitized. |
| `success_redirect_url` | body | string | no | After the final step, send the visitor to this absolute http(s) URL or root-relative path (for example a booking or thank-you page) instead of showing success_message. Pass an empty string to clear. |
| `actions` | body | object[] | no | The complete list of actions after a submission (replaces the current list): email notifications, webhooks, app actions (get_form_capabilities lists the types and their config). Read the form first and send back the actions you keep. Emails send through the provider set with set_email_settings. Requires admin permission, like the portal. |
| `option_sources` | body | object[] | no | Live select/radio options from an installed app. Discover types with get_form_capabilities; admin permission required. |
| `allow_back` | body | boolean \| null | no | Multi-step forms: show a Back button from the second step; it returns to the previous step in the browser with the answers kept. Default (omitted or null): on from render version 5, off before. |
| `show_progress` | body | boolean \| "text" \| "bar" | no | Multi-step forms: true or "text" shows "Step X of Y", "bar" a slim progress bar (with the same text for screen readers). Off by default; false turns it off. |
| `target` | body | object | no | Admin-only: bind to a declared POST route of an enabled app installation. Read its authenticated guide first. |

### `update_form`

`PATCH /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/forms/{form_id}`

Permission: `write`

Patch a form. Provide only what you want to change. Passing `steps` replaces the whole step list; passing `fields` (sugar for simple forms) replaces the whole step list with ONE static step built from them. Passing `actions` replaces the email notifications and webhooks (admin). The existing form_id is immutable.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `form_id` | path | string | yes |  |
| `patch` | body | object | yes |  |

### `delete_form`

`DELETE /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/forms/{form_id}`

Permission: `write`

Delete a form. Existing submissions are preserved by default — pass delete_submissions: true to also drop them.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `form_id` | path | string | yes |  |
| `delete_submissions` | query | boolean | no |  |

### `list_form_intake_responses`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/forms/{form_id}/intake-responses`

Permission: `read`

Administrator-only private questionnaire responses linked to one Page. Includes partial answers and notification status; never use for public profile content. Installation access requires forms:intake:read and is restricted to its own form.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `form_id` | path | string | yes |  |
| `page_id` | query | string | yes |  |
| `after_id` | query | string | no |  |

### `retry_form_intake_notification`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/forms/{form_id}/intake-responses`

Permission: `admin`

Explicitly retry one private questionnaire notification after a confirmed failure, or dispatch its pending outbox event. Never resends accepted, in-flight or uncertain delivery. Requires site administrator access; installation callers need forms:intake:read and email:send.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `form_id` | path | string | yes |  |

### `list_form_submissions`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/forms/{form_id}/submissions`

Permission: `read`

List submissions received for a form, newest first, cursor-paginated (cap 200 per page). Admins also see each submission's webhook delivery status. Visitor IP addresses are not stored or returned; completed submissions past the site's form_submission_retention_days (read_site_settings) are deleted and never listed. Use this to help a customer triage inbound contact / lead submissions; read_form_submission reads one.

| `form_id` | path | string | yes |  |

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/forms/{form_id}/submissions/{submission_id}`

Permission: `read`

Read one submission of a form by id (from list_form_submissions): the submitted values, status (partial or complete), step and timestamps, with expires_at when the submission is due for deletion. Admins also see its webhook delivery status, as in the portal.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `form_id` | path | string | yes |  |
| `submission_id` | path | string | yes |  |

`DELETE /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/forms/{form_id}/submissions/{submission_id}`

Permission: `write`

Delete a single submission from a form's inbox. Use this to remove individual entries (test submissions, spam) without touching the rest — delete_form with delete_submissions is the only way to bulk-delete. Get submission ids from list_form_submissions.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `form_id` | path | string | yes |  |
| `submission_id` | path | string | yes |  |

## Site: Indexing diagnostics

### `check_site_indexing`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/indexing-diagnostics`

Permission: `read`

Probe the site's recorded fallback and live production origins and report indexing safety. Keeps X-Robots-Tag, HTML robots meta, and robots.txt crawl policy separate. expectation_reason identifies fallback_protection, platform_robots_blocked, sitewide_noindex or public_site. Customer publishing without a future website host intentionally blocks indexing even when sitewide_noindex is false; this is expected, not an error. Fallback URLs must expose the documented edge noindex header. Each target also records whose page was read: serving_publication (the X-Typeroll-Publication header, else /.well-known/typeroll/publication.json), serving_typeroll and provider_hint (a likely previous host named by a well-known header such as x-kinsta-cache). For customer publishing the current publication is expected; when another host or another publication answers, serving_typeroll is false, matches_expected is false and an issue explains it, because the robots findings then describe that other host. A previous host using Cloudflare for SaaS (for example Kinsta) outranks the customer's own DNS until the domain is removed from that host's dashboard. Use before launch and after changing domains or indexing settings.

## Site: Insights

### `get_site_insights`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/insights`

Permission: `read`

Read Analytics insights over the last 7, 30, or 90 days: traffic, AI-assistant referrals, and first-party conversion events grouped by event, destination, source, and campaign. Traffic is powered by Cloudflare Web Analytics; conversions come from validated attribution-funnel click events. The response carries a traffic `status`: "ok" with numbers, "no_data" for a linked site without traffic, or "app_disabled" / "not_configured" / "no_site_tag" / "connection_required" / "access_required" / "account_mismatch" / "provider_error" with a `reason` ({code, message, next_step, settings_url}). Traffic is read from the same Cloudflare account the beacon belongs to (`account`): the site's Hosting Group account for customer publishing, the installation's account otherwise. Conversion data can still be present when the traffic provider is unavailable.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `days` | query | number \| number \| number | no | Look-back window in days (default 30). |

## Site: Integrations

### `get_form_spam_protection`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/integrations/form-spam-protection`

Permission: `read`

Read the site's Cloudflare Turnstile setup for forms: provider, public site_key, secret_key masked as { set: true }, and enforced_forms (forms whose published pages have sent a verified Turnstile answer and now require one). provider is null when Turnstile is off. Admin permission required.

### `set_form_spam_protection`

`PUT /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/integrations/form-spam-protection`

Permission: `admin`

Turn on Cloudflare Turnstile for every form on the site, against bots that fill in forms in a real browser. First create a Turnstile widget in the site owner's Cloudflare dashboard (Turnstile → Add widget, mode Managed, with the site's website hostnames), then pass its site key and secret key. The secret is checked with Cloudflare, encrypted and never returned; omit secret_key to keep the stored one for the same site_key. Publish the site afterwards: forms render the widget only after publishing. Each form keeps accepting submissions without Turnstile until its republished pages send the first verified answer, then requires it. Forms that post to an app or Extension are not covered. Admin permission required.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `site_key` | body | string | yes | The Turnstile widget's site key (public). |
| `secret_key` | body | string | no | The Turnstile widget's secret key. Required for a new site_key. |

### `delete_form_spam_protection`

`DELETE /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/integrations/form-spam-protection`

Permission: `admin`

Turn off Turnstile for the site's forms and delete the stored secret. Submissions are accepted without Turnstile at once; republish to remove the widget from pages. Admin permission required.

### `get_email_settings`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/integrations/email`

Permission: `read`

Read the site's outgoing email connector (the provider form notifications send through): type, from, reply_to and config with secrets masked as { set: true }, plus every available provider with its field schema and whether the server can store secrets (crypto_configured). email is null when nothing is connected. Admin permission required.

### `set_email_settings`

`PUT /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/integrations/email`

Permission: `admin`

Connect or change the site's outgoing email provider, like Settings → Email &amp; notifications in the portal. Read get_email_settings first for the provider field schema. Examples: postmark config { server_token, message_stream? }; smtp config { host, port?, secure?, user?, password? }. Secrets are encrypted server-side and never returned; omit a secret (or send the masked value) to keep the stored one. Then call send_test_email. Admin permission required.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | body | string | yes | Provider type from get_email_settings providers, e.g. "postmark" or "smtp". |
| `from` | body | string | yes | Sender, e.g. "Acme &lt;hello@acme.com&gt;". Must be a sender the provider accepts. |
| `reply_to` | body | string | no | Optional default Reply-To address. |
| `config` | body | object | no | Provider fields keyed by the field schema. |

## Site: Lifecycle

### `archive_site`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/lifecycle`

Permission: `admin`

Archive (retire) this site, the same action as Settings → Archive site in the portal. An archived site stays readable but refuses every write and publish until restored; the last published output keeps serving. Refused with 409 while a custom domain is still live or verified — move or remove the domain first. Requires an admin key of the organization that OWNS the site (a site-scoped key or the owner organization's org key); a key that reaches the site through a share is refused. Idempotent. Confirm with the user before calling.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `reason` | body | string | no | Why the site is retired; shown in the portal. |

### `restore_site`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/lifecycle`

Permission: `admin`

Restore an archived site so it accepts writes and publishing again, the same action as Restore in the portal. Same permission as archive_site (owner-organization admin). Idempotent: restoring an active site succeeds without change.

### `get_media_preparation`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/media/preparation`

Permission: `read`

Read background image preparation progress, including the build_job_id of a running preparation job on the organization build engine. unreadable_media lists library images whose stored file does not decode; preparation skips them, so upload a working copy. A round stopped by a passing condition (engine update, runner not started, step time limit, interrupted transfer) never ends the job: it starts again after 5 minutes, doubling up to an hour, shown as retry { attempt, next_at } with error_code. When the job fails, error names the cause, with error_code and failed_build_task. Originals and prepared draft variants remain private. Requires site access.

Permission: `read`

Read one media item's metadata by id.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |

| `media_id` | path | string | yes |  |

### `create_upload_url`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/media/upload-url`

Permission: `write`

Mint a 5-min signed PUT URL for direct-to-R2 upload. After the upload completes, the CDN url is what you reference in &lt;img src="…"&gt;. REQUIRED follow-up: call `finalize_media` after the PUT succeeds — without it the original ships with no Cache-Control (Lighthouse will flag it) and no responsive variants get generated. The response carries `finalize_url` as a reminder. This signed-PUT path is the INTEGRITY-SAFE way to upload bytes from disk or a generated asset — a direct `curl --data-binary @file` sends the bytes straight to R2 without transcribing them through the model, so it can't be corrupted the way a large `upload_media_inline` base64 blob can (ESPECIALLY use this, not inline, for SVG/logos). For a public source URL, `upload_media_from_url` is the one-call equivalent; reserve `upload_media_inline` for tiny payloads only.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `filename` | body | string | yes | Should end in an extension of content_type (e.g. logo.png with image/png). When the extension is missing or belongs to another type, the type's extension is appended (logo → logo.png, photo.html → photo.html.png); the response returns the stored filename. Unsupported types answer 415. |
| `content_type` | body | string | yes | e.g. "image/png", "image/jpeg", "application/pdf". SVGs are sanitized at finalize; an SVG that cannot be sanitized is refused. |
| `size` | body | integer | no |  |
| `alt_text` | body | string | no |  |

### `upload_media_from_url`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/media/import`

Permission: `write`

Fetch an image (or PDF) from any public URL and push it to the site's media library in one call. The organization's media transfer Worker downloads the source from verified public HTTP(S) destinations straight into the organization's storage; private addresses and unsafe redirects are refused. Integrity-safe: the bytes are streamed, never transcribed as base64 through the model, so (unlike a large `upload_media_inline` payload) they can't be silently corrupted in transit. Returns { media_id, cdn_url, filename, finalize }. Each upload queues image preparation (finalize.preparation): one job per site on the organization's shared build engine, started once uploads have been quiet for 30 s (at most 5 min after the first), so a series of uploads shares one job. get_media_preparation returns its build_job_id; let it finish, like any other active build, before publishing another site of the organization.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source_url` | body | string | yes | Public URL to download the image from. |
| `filename` | body | string | no | Override the filename used on R2. Defaults to the last path segment of source_url. When its extension does not match the content type, the type's extension is appended; the response returns the stored filename. |
| `content_type` | body | string | no | Override the inferred content type (e.g. when source_url has no extension). |
| `alt_text` | body | string | no |  |

### `upload_media_batch_from_urls`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/media/import`

Permission: `write`

Upload 1–50 public images/PDFs (max 25 MiB each) in one MCP call. Uses the same integrity-safe download → signed PUT → finalize pipeline as upload_media_from_url, with four concurrent workers. Returns one result per source URL; individual failures do not abort the batch. Uploads queue image preparation as upload_media_from_url describes; consecutive batches share one preparation job while each starts within 30 s of the previous one.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | body | object[] | yes |  |

### `upload_media_inline`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/media/upload-url`

Permission: `write`

Upload an image (or PDF) from base64-encoded bytes. ⚠️ Use ONLY for tiny payloads (a few KB). The base64 string crosses the model/tool boundary as text, where a larger blob can be SILENTLY CORRUPTED in transit — a few mutated chars yield a broken-but-valid-looking file that uploads with no error and the right size, and only fails when rendered (this has bitten a ~12KB logo SVG: half the wordmark vanished). For anything non-trivial, and ALWAYS for SVG/logos or assets you generated, prefer create_upload_url + a direct curl --data-binary PUT of the file bytes (bytes never transcribed → verified byte-identical), or upload_media_from_url (bytes fetched from a URL). After uploading any generated asset, VERIFY it (render it, or byte-diff against the source) before referencing it. Returns { media_id, cdn_url, filename }.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `filename` | body | string | yes | When its extension does not match content_type, the type's extension is appended; the response returns the stored filename. |
| `content_type` | body | string | yes | e.g. "image/png", "image/jpeg", "application/pdf" |
| `data_base64` | body | string | yes | The file bytes, base64-encoded (without a data: URL prefix). |
| `alt_text` | body | string | no |  |

### `update_media`

`PATCH /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/media/{media_id}`

Permission: `write`

Patch a media item's alt text, filename or public path. A rename must be correct: a new filename or public path must end in an extension matching the file's type, and nothing is appended (400 media_extension_mismatch otherwise). A public path change is applied at the next publication.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `media_id` | path | string | yes |  |
| `alt_text` | body | string | no |  |
| `filename` | body | string | no |  |
| `public_path` | body | string \| null | no | Optional stable path such as /wp-content/uploads/2023/photo.jpg. Applied at the next build; existing public image URLs stay available. |

### `generate_image_variants`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/media/{media_id}/generate-variants`

Permission: `write`

Run the build-time srcset pipeline for one image: produces webp + avif variants at 320 / 640 / 1024 / 1920 (skipping upscales), uploads them to R2 alongside the original, and patches the media doc with a variants[] array. Synchronous; takes ~1-5s per image. Skips PDFs and non-image media without erroring. NOTE: prefer `finalize_media` for new uploads — it does this PLUS sets immutable Cache-Control on the original. Use this tool only for surgical variant reruns.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `media_id` | path | string | yes |  |

### `finalize_media`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/media/{media_id}/finalize`

Permission: `write`

Post-upload finalize for a single image: (1) applies immutable Cache-Control (public, max-age=31536000) to the R2 original via in-place CopyObject so the CDN caches it for a year, and (2) generates AVIF/WebP responsive variants if not already present. Call this immediately after a successful upload (the presigned PUT does NOT set cache headers — without finalize, Cloudflare defaults to ~4h and every visit re-fetches the original). Idempotent: safe to call twice. Skips variant work when variants already exist on the doc. INTEGRITY: the response is { ok, result: { sha256, size_bytes, ... } }; read result.sha256 and result.size_bytes for the stored original — compare against your source file to catch transit corruption before referencing the asset. Better: pass expected_sha256 (hash the file yourself first, e.g. `shasum -a 256 file`) and the server rejects a mismatch with a 422 so corrupted bytes never get blessed with immutable cache headers. Truncated SVGs are rejected outright.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `media_id` | path | string | yes |  |
| `expected_sha256` | body | string | no | sha256 (hex) of the SOURCE file. Mismatch with the stored bytes → 422 (re-upload via create_upload_url + direct PUT). |

### `finalize_all_media`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/media/finalize-all`

Permission: `write`

Backfill version of finalize_media: walks the entire media library, applies cache headers + variant generation to every item missing them. Use this once on legacy sites to fix Lighthouse "cache lifetimes" + "image delivery" warnings in one go. Synchronous, can take minutes on large libraries (~1-5s per image needing variants, ~50ms for cache-only). Idempotent.

### `suggest_alt_text_context`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/media/{media_id}/alt-text-context`

Permission: `write`

Get everything you need to generate good alt-text for a media item: the image URL, a tuned SEO/accessibility prompt, the site's content language, and the list of pages where the image is used (with the nearest heading per use site). YOU run the actual vision call with your own model — this endpoint does NOT generate text. After you decide on alt-text, save it with update_media.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `media_id` | path | string | yes |  |

### `purge_site_media`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/media/purge`

Permission: `admin`

Permanently delete every media object and record of an ARCHIVED site (archive_site first; an active site returns 409). Irreversible — the step before retiring a site for good, same as the portal action. Requires an admin key of the organization that owns the site; shared access is refused. Returns counts; HTTP 207 with `failed` lists objects that could not be removed (their records are kept) — call again to retry exactly those. Confirm with the user before calling.

### `delete_media`

`DELETE /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/media/{media_id}`

Permission: `write`

Delete a media item's metadata. (R2 object cleanup is a separate ops task.)

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `media_id` | path | string | yes |  |

## Site: Menus

### `list_menus`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/menus`

Permission: `read`

List the site's menus (WordPress-style menus with locations): each with its id, name, locations, auto_add_pages, items and updated_at. Check this before building a header or footer: a new site starts with a `primary` menu (location primary, Home, auto_add_pages on) and a `footer` menu. A menu has an id, a name, optional `locations` and a tree of `items` at most 3 levels deep (top level, submenu, and a third level that makes a wide submenu in columns). Item types: `page` (page_id; links by page id, so the label and address follow renames and moves, and an unpublished or deleted page drops out with a warning; `label` overrides the title), `url` (href and label; an external address, a path or an #anchor), `children` (page_id; lists that page's published child pages automatically: with a label they form a submenu under it, without one they sit in place) and `heading` (label only, no link; a column title in a wide submenu). Any item may set `description` (a short line in submenus), `icon` and `link_rel`. Items with `children` get a submenu. Locations: `primary` (header), `footer` and `mobile`, or another short lowercase name; one menu per location per site. `auto_add_pages: true` appends new top-level published pages (other than the home page) to the end automatically. To show a menu, use a `core/navigation_links` block with data { source: "menu", menu: "location:primary" } (or a menu id) and optionally `submenus`: auto (dropdown in a row, accordion in a column and the mobile drawer), dropdown, accordion, expanded or none. It needs render version 15 (read_site_settings → render.version; raise it with tr-upgrade-rendering).

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | query | string | no | Branch id to target. Omit for main. An id that does not name a version of this Site is refused with 404 — it is never answered about main instead. |

### `read_menu`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/menus/{menu_id}`

Permission: `read`

Read one menu with its whole item tree and updated_at. Pass that updated_at as expected_updated_at to update_menu so a save made in between is not overwritten.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `menu_id` | path | string | yes |  |
| `version` | query | string | no | Branch id to target. Omit for main. An id that does not name a version of this Site is refused with 404 — it is never answered about main instead. |

### `update_menu`

`PUT /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/menus/{menu_id}`

Permission: `write`

Create a menu or replace a whole menu (name, locations, auto_add_pages and the full item tree). To change an existing menu: read_menu, edit the tree, and send it back with expected_updated_at set to the updated_at you read; a save by someone else in between returns 409. Without menu_id, or with a menu_id that does not exist yet, the menu is created. Every save is validated as a whole and keeps the previous menu as a revision; an invalid menu returns `errors` with the path of each problem (for example items[0].href). Link pages with type "page" and their page_id (from list_pages), not with url items, so renames follow; use a "children" item for an automatic submenu of a page's child pages. Menus are saved directly (no working copy) and reach the live site with the next publication. To add one item, add_menu_item is simpler. A menu has an id, a name, optional `locations` and a tree of `items` at most 3 levels deep (top level, submenu, and a third level that makes a wide submenu in columns). Item types: `page` (page_id; links by page id, so the label and address follow renames and moves, and an unpublished or deleted page drops out with a warning; `label` overrides the title), `url` (href and label; an external address, a path or an #anchor), `children` (page_id; lists that page's published child pages automatically: with a label they form a submenu under it, without one they sit in place) and `heading` (label only, no link; a column title in a wide submenu). Any item may set `description` (a short line in submenus), `icon` and `link_rel`. Items with `children` get a submenu. Locations: `primary` (header), `footer` and `mobile`, or another short lowercase name; one menu per location per site. `auto_add_pages: true` appends new top-level published pages (other than the home page) to the end automatically. To show a menu, use a `core/navigation_links` block with data { source: "menu", menu: "location:primary" } (or a menu id) and optionally `submenus`: auto (dropdown in a row, accordion in a column and the mobile drawer), dropdown, accordion, expanded or none. It needs render version 15 (read_site_settings → render.version; raise it with tr-upgrade-rendering).

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `menu_id` | path | string | no | The menu to replace or create. Omit to create a menu whose id is derived from the name. |
| `name` | body | string | yes | Shown in the portal, e.g. "Main menu". |
| `locations` | body | string[] | no | primary, footer, mobile or another short lowercase name. Omit to keep none; [] clears them. |
| `auto_add_pages` | body | boolean | no | Append new top-level published pages automatically. |
| `items` | body | object[] | yes | The whole item tree, at most 3 levels deep and 200 items. |
| `expected_updated_at` | body | string | no | The updated_at from read_menu or list_menus. Required to replace an existing menu. |
| `version` | query | string | no | Branch id to target. Omit for main. An id that does not name a version of this Site is refused with 404 — it is never answered about main instead. |

### `add_menu_item`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/menus/{menu_id}`

Permission: `write`

Append one item to a menu, at the top level or under a parent item (parent_item_id), and save it. Reads the menu and saves it with its updated_at, so a concurrent save is refused with 409 rather than lost. Example: { menu_id: "primary", item: { type: "page", page_id: "about" } } or a submenu entry { menu_id: "primary", parent_item_id: "services", item: { type: "url", href: "https://shop.example.com", label: "Shop" } }. Use type "page" with a page_id (it follows renames), "children" for the page's child pages as an automatic submenu, "url" for other addresses and "heading" for a column title. Menus are at most 3 levels deep. Returns the saved menu and the new item's id. To restructure or remove items, use read_menu and update_menu.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `menu_id` | path | string | yes |  |
| `item` | query | object | yes |  |
| `parent_item_id` | query | string | no | Put the item in this item's submenu (as its last child). Omit for the top level. |
| `position` | query | integer | no | Index to insert at among its siblings. Default: at the end. |
| `version` | query | string | no | Branch id to target. Omit for main. An id that does not name a version of this Site is refused with 404 — it is never answered about main instead. |

### `delete_menu`

`DELETE /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/menus/{menu_id}`

Permission: `write`

Delete a menu. A navigation block that shows it (by id or by its location) then renders an empty list until another menu fills the location. Check where it is shown first with find_menu_usage. Takes effect at the next publication.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `menu_id` | path | string | yes |  |
| `version` | query | string | no | Branch id to target. Omit for main. An id that does not name a version of this Site is refused with 404 — it is never answered about main instead. |

### `find_menu_usage`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/menus/{menu_id}/usage`

Permission: `read`

Where a menu is shown: the global blocks (header, footer, others), pages and page templates whose core/navigation_links block has source "menu" and names this menu by id or by one of its locations (location:primary), saved or in a draft. Read it before deleting a menu or moving its location.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `menu_id` | path | string | yes |  |
| `version` | query | string | no | Branch id to target. Omit for main. An id that does not name a version of this Site is refused with 404 — it is never answered about main instead. |

## Site: Migration preflight

### `get_migration_readiness`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/migration-preflight`

Permission: `read`

Preflight for an import: is this site actually ready to receive a migration? CALL THIS FIRST, before moving any content. Every check exists because its failure is INVISIBLE afterwards — the pages import, the previews render, the customer signs off, and something is quietly wrong. Pass proposed compositions to also inventory their block, field, and native-feature dependencies before implementation. A generic custom block, raw-HTML fallback, per-instance CSS workaround, missing block type, or missing declared field returns waiting_for_native_support and makes ready=false. Do not implement those workarounds; report the gap and wait for Core support. Business-specific custom blocks are allowed only when explicitly listed. Infrastructure warnings cover the pre-cutover verification URL, form notification email and whether the target has a design to rebuild INTO.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source_url` | body | string | no | The site you are migrating FROM, e.g. "https://oldsite.com". When given, the source is probed too: unreachable or bot-blocked (403/429) is a BLOCKER because an import from a host that refuses our requests produces empty pages, and whether /wp-json answers is reported as a warning (without it the importer must scrape HTML and loses ACF/custom fields). |
| `compositions` | body | object[] | no | Proposed block compositions before build. Standard blocks first, reviewed reusable custom types next, raw HTML only as a documented last resort. reviewed_custom_block_types and reviewed_html_blocks record exact choices and reasons, not proof of visual quality. Missing types/fields still block readiness. |

## Site: Migration report

### `record_migration_seo_acceptance`

`PUT /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/migration-report/seo-acceptance`

Permission: `write`

Record the reviewed SEO/content parity evidence used by the launch report. This does not run the audit. Supply the exact source/target origins, checked timestamp, dataset description, page count and difference counts. Also supply fidelity: desktop/mobile review against the source (preserve) or approved design (renew), shared-data checks, integration checks and evidence notes identifying the intent and approved differences. HTTP 200 is not visual acceptance. status=accepted requires unresolved=0. Re-run and record new evidence after every deploy.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | body | "accepted" \| "rejected" | yes |  |
| `checked_at` | body | string | yes |  |
| `dataset` | body | string | yes |  |
| `source_origin` | body | string | yes |  |
| `target_origin` | body | string | yes |  |
| `checked_pages` | body | integer | yes |  |
| `differences` | body | object | yes |  |
| `fidelity` | body | object | no |  |
| `notes` | body | string | no |  |

### `get_migration_launch_report`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/migration-report`

Permission: `read`

Return the launch decision report with separate inventory, exclusion-reason, internal-link, deployed URL parity, deploy freshness, reviewed SEO/content parity, migration fidelity and script requirements. scripts lists copied source-platform scripts (WordPress plugins, theme, jQuery, page builders, cookie plugins), tracking code outside the consent gate, and analytics/advertising integrations without the cookie banner; each blocks launch. launch_ready is false when any evidence is absent, incomplete, failed, targets an old origin, or predates the latest hosted deploy. Use this final gate instead of treating zero unhandled URLs as launch readiness.

## Site: Migration urls

### `import_sitemap`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/migration-urls/import-sitemap`

Permission: `write`

Import an explicit sitemap URL into the migration URL inventory. Sitemap indexes are followed recursively; URLs outside source_origin are rejected and reported.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | body | string | yes | Absolute URL of a sitemap or sitemap index. |
| `include_wordpress` | body | boolean | no | Also enumerate public WordPress REST pages/posts/types. No helper installation required; incomplete discovery is reported. |
| `crawl_pages` | body | integer | no | With include_wordpress, crawl up to this many source pages for same-origin legacy links. Default 0; bounded discovery is not an authoritative old-slug export. |
| `source_origin` | body | string | no | Expected legacy-site origin. Defaults to the sitemap origin. |

### `import_gsc_performance`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/migration-urls/import-gsc`

Permission: `write`

Import URL metrics from Google Search Console. Use property for a direct server-side Search Console API query, or csv for the manual export fallback. URL fragments are stripped, duplicate metrics are summed, and previously unknown URLs enter the inventory as unhandled.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `property` | body | string | no | Search Console property, e.g. https://example.com/ or sc-domain:example.com. |
| `months` | body | integer | no |  |
| `csv` | body | string | no | Raw Search Console Pages CSV export. |

### `list_migration_urls`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/migration-urls`

Permission: `read`

The legacy site's URL inventory with LIVE coverage status. Every entry is classified on read against the site's current pages + redirects: `migrated` (a Page answers at that path), `redirected` (a redirect rule covers it), `excluded` (signed off as an intentional 404), `matched_draft` (a saved but unpublished Page owns the path; not launch-ready), `unhandled` (nothing covers it — the work list). Returns a summary over the whole inventory plus a page of entries, sorted worst-first then by GSC clicks. Use `status: "unhandled"` to get exactly what's left to do before cutover. Coverage is computed, never stored, so it's current the moment you create a redirect.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | query | "migrated" \| "redirected" \| "excluded" \| "unhandled" \| "matched_draft" | no | Only return entries with this coverage status. |
| `limit` | query | integer | no | Default 200. |
| `offset` | query | integer | no |  |

### `add_migration_urls`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/migration-urls`

Permission: `write`

Add old-site URLs to the inventory in bulk (up to 2000 per call). This is how the inventory gets populated outside the in-portal WordPress migration: walk the old sitemap.xml, a GSC export, or a crawl, and post what you found. Idempotent — re-posting a known URL merges its `source` label instead of duplicating. Pass `source_origin` when the site you're inventorying has its own domain: absolute URLs from a different origin are then REJECTED rather than silently folded in, which is what keeps a ten-domain multisite migration from pouring domain B's `/kontakt` into domain A's inventory. Rejected entries come back with a reason — nothing is dropped silently.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `urls` | body | object[] | yes |  |
| `source` | body | string | no | Default source label for entries that omit one. |
| `source_origin` | body | string | no | Origin of the old site, e.g. "https://old.example.com". Rejects absolute URLs from other origins. |

### `update_migration_url`

`PATCH /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/migration-urls/{url_id}`

Permission: `write`

Annotate one inventory entry. `excluded: true` is the sign-off that this URL is MEANT to 404 after cutover — it moves the entry out of the "unhandled" work list without inventing a redirect for it. Also accepts notes and GSC metrics. The url_id is the entry id from list_migration_urls (the path with slashes replaced by underscores).

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url_id` | path | string | yes |  |
| `excluded` | body | boolean | no |  |
| `notes` | body | string | no |  |
| `gsc_clicks` | body | number | no |  |
| `gsc_impressions` | body | number | no |  |

### `update_migration_urls`

`PATCH /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/migration-urls`

Permission: `write`

Apply one shared patch to many inventory entries in a single API request. Select either `ids` (up to 2000) or `where: { source }`, never both. This is the migration-scale path for decisions such as “every wordpress-redirect-guess URL is an intentional 404”; it avoids hundreds of rate-limited PATCH calls. Returns matched/updated/unchanged counts, unknown ids, and the refreshed coverage summary.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ids` | body | string[] | no |  |
| `where` | body | object | no |  |
| `patch` | body | object | yes |  |

### `delete_migration_url`

`DELETE /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/migration-urls/{url_id}`

Permission: `write`

Remove an entry from the inventory entirely. Use for junk the crawl picked up (session URLs, faceted duplicates). To record a deliberate 404 instead, prefer update_migration_url with excluded: true — that keeps the decision visible in the coverage report.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url_id` | path | string | yes |  |

### `repair_migration_plain_text`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/migration-urls/repair-plain-text`

Permission: `write`

Repair legacy WordPress entity encoding and HTML markup in fields whose contract is plain text. ONLY title, seo_title, seo_description and excerpt are eligible; rich content, slugs, paths and URLs are never changed. ALWAYS run the dry-run first (the default), show every returned before/after diff and conflict to the user, and obtain approval before calling again with dry_run:false. Existing working copies are skipped so another editor's draft cannot be overwritten or accidentally saved. save:false stages working copies for portal review; save:true commits through the normal revision and validation path.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `scope` | body | "pages" \| "all" | no | Defaults to all. |
| `fields` | body | "title" \| "seo_title" \| "seo_description" \| "excerpt"[] | no | Narrow the fixed plain-text allowlist. |
| `page_ids` | body | string[] | no |  |
| `content_type` | body | string | no |  |
| `dry_run` | body | boolean | no | Defaults to true. Set false only after the user reviews the dry-run. |
| `save` | body | boolean | no | With dry_run:false, commit repaired working copies immediately. Defaults to false. |
| `diff_limit` | body | integer | no | Exact field diffs returned; default 500. |
| `version` | query | string | no | Branch id to target. Omit for main. An id that does not name a version of this Site is refused with 404 — it is never answered about main instead. |

### `verify_migration_urls`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/migration-urls/verify`

Permission: `write`

Inventories over 500 URLs: one call checks at most 500 and stores no launch evidence (the response then has evidence_stored: false and next_step); run start_workflow with type url_parity to check every URL and record the evidence. Pre-cutover parity check: actually REQUEST every observed inventory path against the new site and report what it answers. Slash-equivalent paths share one inventory row but remain separate checks through `observed_paths`, so `summary.checked` can exceed the normalized inventory count. list_migration_urls tells you what the data says; this tells you what the server does — a redirect pointing at an unpublished page, a typo'd path, a missing slash variant, or a redirect loop all read as "handled" in coverage and as a 404 to Googlebot. Runs against the site's live domain by default; before cutover pass the temporary address the site publishes to as target_origin. The response is compact by default: the full summary plus only `missing`, `broken_redirect`, and `error` rows; successful rows are counted but omitted. Pass `verdicts` for an exact result filter or `include_successes: true` for every row. Canonical trailing-slash normalization counts as `ok`, not `ok_redirect`. A query-string rule (published as an inline script, also from 404.html) is followed and counts as `ok_redirect` with `client_redirect: true`. Also stamps verified/last_checked on redirect rules it exercised. Deploy before running this — it tests the DEPLOYED site, not your drafts.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `target_origin` | body | string | no | Origin to test, e.g. the temporary address the site publishes to before cutover. Defaults to the site's live domain. |
| `source_origin` | body | string | no | Old site origin, e.g. "https://old.example.com". |
| `check_source` | body | boolean | no | Also request each path on the OLD site (requires source_origin), so a URL that already 404s upstream is distinguishable from one the migration lost. Doubles the request count. |
| `statuses` | body | "migrated" \| "redirected" \| "excluded" \| "unhandled" \| "matched_draft"[] | no | Only check entries with these coverage statuses. Default: all — "migrated" is exactly the claim this check exists to falsify. |
| `verdicts` | body | "ok" \| "ok_redirect" \| "missing" \| "broken_redirect" \| "error" \| "excluded"[] | no | Only return rows with these verdicts. The summary still covers every checked URL. |
| `include_successes` | body | boolean | no | Return all rows when verdicts is omitted. Default false: successful/excluded rows are summarized but omitted. |
| `limit` | body | integer | no | Max URLs per run (default 150). `truncated: true` in the response means there are more. |
| `concurrency` | body | integer | no |  |

## Site: Packages

### `export_package`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/packages/export`

Permission: `write`

Export part of the site, or the whole site, as a Typeroll package (.typeroll) and get a signed download address valid for one hour (download_url, filename, bytes, sha256, expires_at, warnings). A package belongs to no organization: it carries no organization or site ids, and its media files (and font files the author may pass on) travel inside it, so anyone can import it into their own site, for example a template pack bought from someone else. Media references in content become `typeroll-media:<id>` tokens and app blocks are named by their app, not the site's installation. selection.kind "collection" holds what you choose: block_templates, page_templates, global_blocks (free global blocks) and block_types as id lists or "all", styles "used" (default) or "all", design (colours, typography, scales, content widths, font roles and element styles), menus, site_fields (definitions) and demo_media (media ids to mark as demo content the buyer replaces). Global blocks, block types and styles the content uses come along by themselves; links to this site's pages become plain addresses. kind "site" holds everything (pages, header and footer, menus, site fields with values, every style and the design) and requires admin. fonts: { families, redistributable_confirmed: true } adds uploaded font files only when the user confirmed their licence allows passing them on; catalog families need no files. Requires write permission.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `selection` | body | object | yes |  |
| `meta` | body | object | yes |  |
| `version` | body | string | no | Branch id to target. Omit for main. An id that does not name a version of this Site is refused with 404 — it is never answered about main instead. |

### `inspect_package`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/packages/inspect`

Permission: `read`

Read a Typeroll package and show what importing it into the site would do, without changing anything: the package (name, version, author, licence, counts), its signature (verified with the publisher when a trusted publisher signed it; unsigned or unknown otherwise), the plan (per style, block type, template, global block, menu, page and media file: create, reuse, rename or replace, with the id maps), warnings, errors that would stop the import, and needs (admin, font_licence). Styles are never mapped to the site's "nearest" styles: every style the imported content uses is created on the site. A style is reused only when the site has one with the same id and the same definition; a differing one is created under a new id (hero-2, named "Hero (imported)") and the imported content is rewritten to it. Block types, templates, global blocks, menus and pages that collide get new ids the same way. options.design: "content" (default: the blocks and the styles they use), "styles" (also the package's other class styles) or "full" (also the element styles body/h1–h6/link replacing the site's, colours, typography, scales, content widths and font roles; requires admin). Font files in the package are added to the Fonts library only with options.font_licence_confirmed: true, which means the user confirmed the font licence allows use on this site; ask the user, never assume it. options.fonts: false leaves the fonts out. Adobe Fonts, Bunny Fonts and Fontshare kits never transfer: only the family names, with a warning. Run it before import_package and show the user the plan.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data_base64` | body | string | no | The .typeroll file, base64-encoded (at most 32 MB). Send this or source_url. |
| `source_url` | body | string | no | An https:// address to download the package from (up to 200 MB), instead of data_base64. |
| `options` | body | object | no |  |
| `version` | body | string | no | Branch id to target. Omit for main. An id that does not name a version of this Site is refused with 404 — it is never answered about main instead. |

### `import_package`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/packages/import`

Permission: `write`

Import a Typeroll package into the site: media first (into the Media library, reusing files with the same bytes; demo files are marked for replacement before publication), then fonts, block types, design and styles, global blocks, block templates (with where they came from), page templates, menus, site fields and, for a site package, pages. Returns a report of what was created, reused, renamed and replaced. Styles are never mapped to the site's "nearest" styles: every style the imported content uses is created on the site. A style is reused only when the site has one with the same id and the same definition; a differing one is created under a new id (hero-2, named "Hero (imported)") and the imported content is rewritten to it. Block types, templates, global blocks, menus and pages that collide get new ids the same way. options.design: "content" (default: the blocks and the styles they use), "styles" (also the package's other class styles) or "full" (also the element styles body/h1–h6/link replacing the site's, colours, typography, scales, content widths and font roles; requires admin). Font files in the package are added to the Fonts library only with options.font_licence_confirmed: true, which means the user confirmed the font licence allows use on this site; ask the user, never assume it. options.fonts: false leaves the fonts out. Adobe Fonts, Bunny Fonts and Fontshare kits never transfer: only the family names, with a warning. Requires write permission; admin for design "full" or when the import adds fonts or settings pages. The whole plan is checked before anything is written; a write that fails part-way answers package_import_partial with the report of what was written.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data_base64` | body | string | no | The .typeroll file, base64-encoded (at most 32 MB). Send this or source_url. |
| `source_url` | body | string | no | An https:// address to download the package from (up to 200 MB), instead of data_base64. |
| `options` | body | object | yes |  |
| `version` | body | string | no | Branch id to target. Omit for main. An id that does not name a version of this Site is refused with 404 — it is never answered about main instead. |

Permission: `write`

Create a new page. Defaults to blocks mode (same as the portal UI's "New page" button) and seeds the tree with a heading + prose block so the editor is never blank. Pass html_content (or content_mode="html") to opt into raw-HTML mode instead. Slug is derived from the title when omitted. Default status is "draft". Address conflicts: an explicit slug or path that another page already uses (drafts and unsaved drafts included) fails with 409 { code: "slug_in_use" | "path_in_use", details: { page_id, path } } — edit that page or choose another slug; the address is never changed silently. Only a title-derived slug is numbered (e.g. "tack" → "tack-2"), and the response then carries warnings: [{ code: "slug_adjusted", requested, slug, path, conflicting_page_id }]. Homepage convention: pass slug="" (empty string) or omit slug and set title to "Home"; the server stores it under id "home" with slug "". Slug must be a single path segment (no slashes). For nested URLs like /erbjudanden/sommar or /tjanster/design, set the optional `path` field explicitly — e.g. path="/erbjudanden/sommar". For pages with the same schema use a content type with route_template (see tr-blog), but for a small group of bespoke pages sharing a URL prefix, `path` is the right primitive. Returns the created page (blocks for blocks-mode, html_content for html-mode) including `url` (the resolved live URL).

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `write_mode` | body | "editor" \| "import" | no | Default editor. Use import for research/migration seeding so later owner answers outrank it. Fields must explicitly allow import; server assigns provenance. Does not reclassify existing pages. |
| `title` | body | string | yes |  |
| `content_type` | body | string | no | Content type ID; defaults to page. |
| `fields` | body | object | no | Custom field values defined by the content type. |
| `slug` | body | string | no | URL slug — single path segment, no slashes (e.g. "about", "kontakt"). Empty string "" = homepage. For nested URLs set the `path` field explicitly — `slug` stays a leaf id. Already in use → 409 slug_in_use naming the existing page; omit it to derive one from the title (numbered with a slug_adjusted warning on conflict). |
| `path` | body | string | no | Optional explicit URL path for nested pages (e.g. "/erbjudanden/sommar-2026"). When set, takes precedence over slug for routing. Must start with "/", lowercase a-z/0-9/-/_/ only, no "..", no "//", no trailing slash. Slug is still required as the leaf id but two pages CAN share a slug under different paths. |
| `content_mode` | body | "blocks" \| "html" | no | Default "blocks". "blocks" stores a Block[] tree (the modern default — supports the full ~40-block library, page templates, and the responsive system). "html" stores raw markup in html_content (legacy path, still fully supported for imported content or hand-written HTML). Passing html_content without content_mode also opts into "html". |
| `html_content` | body | string | no | Body HTML — only used when content_mode="html". |
| `blocks` | body | any[] | no | Block tree — only used when content_mode="blocks". Omit to get the default heading+prose seed. |
| `status` | body | "draft" \| "review" \| "unlisted" \| "published" | no |  |
| `breadcrumb_label` | body | string \| null | no | Optional short breadcrumb label. Leaves Page title, SEO title and route unchanged; null/empty uses the title. |
| `seo_title` | body | string | no |  |
| `append_seo_suffix` | body | boolean | no | Set false to omit the site default SEO suffix on this page. |
| `seo_description` | body | string | no |  |
| `og_title` | body | string | no |  |
| `og_description` | body | string | no |  |
| `og_image` | body | string | no |  |
| `seo_image_alt` | body | string | no |  |
| `alternates` | body | object[] | no | Cross-domain hreflang cluster: the equivalents of THIS page on sister language sites, as [{ hreflang, href }]. One Typeroll site owns one domain, so a multi-language family (example.se / example.de / example.co.uk) is several sites and the mapping can't be derived — declare it here. List only the OTHER variants; the renderer injects this page's self-reference automatically. hreflang is a BCP-47 tag ("sv", "en-GB") or "x-default"; href must be an absolute http(s) URL. Invalid entries are rejected at write time with the reason, so a half-written cluster never ships. Every page in a cluster must link every other one — write all sides. |
| `schema_type` | body | string | no | Free-form Schema.org type ("Service", "Course", "Product", …) for auto JSON-LD. |
| `kind` | body | "page" \| "article" | no |  |
| `author` | body | string | no |  |
| `language` | body | string | no | BCP-47 tag overriding the site default (e.g. "en" on an otherwise Swedish site). |
| `id` | body | string | no | Page id to use instead of one derived from the address; keeps references such as parent or filter values stable. A taken id fails with 409; it is never replaced. |
| `sort_order` | body | number | no | Manual Page order; lower numbers come first in ascending lists. Content types and listings choose how to sort. |
| `template` | body | string \| null | no | Allowed Page template ID; null uses the content type default. |
| `image_sizes_default` | body | string | no | Per-page default `sizes` for responsive images (e.g. "(max-width: 640px) 360px, 560px"). Overrides the site setting; a per-&lt;img&gt; `sizes` attr still wins. Set when this page's images render narrower than the generic default so the browser stops over-fetching. |
| `custom_css` | body | string | no | Per-page CSS, injected into &lt;head&gt; as a &lt;style&gt; AFTER the site-level custom_css (so it overrides site styling). This is the RIGHT home for page-specific styling — page metadata, not content. Put a page's &lt;style&gt; here instead of stuffing it into a core/html block (which is opaque and un-editable in the visual editor). Syntax errors refuse the write; target s-&lt;style&gt; classes or block custom_class rather than [data-block]/.block-* platform markup. |
| `override_reason` | body | string | no | Why a value the listed business set itself (through its edit link) is being replaced. Required only for those values, as in the portal; the write otherwise returns 409 naming the field. |
| `version` | query | string | no | Branch id to target. Omit for main. An id that does not name a version of this Site is refused with 404 — it is never answered about main instead. |

### `get_page_preview`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/pages/{page_id}/preview`

Permission: `read`

Get the WHOLE page rendered as one self-contained HTML document — header partial + block-rendered body + footer partial, with the site's settings CSS variables, global styles, the tree-shaken block-CSS bundle, block JavaScript, the Extension runtime and the cookie-consent banner all included, exactly as the portal Preview shows it. This is the single artifact for UNDERSTANDING what a page looks like and how its CSS actually cascades (get_page_blocks gives the editable block tree; this gives the rendered result). Returns { rendered_html, internal_links[] }. Pass annotate:true to tag every element with data-block-id + data-block-type so you can map the rendered HTML back to the block to edit. Forms render in preview mode, marked "Preview – nothing is sent": they validate, step through and show the success message (or name the redirect target) in the browser, but store nothing and run no actions — keep the forms runtime as is when building a review copy. For a clickable preview URL use get_preview_link instead.

| `page_id` | path | string | yes |  |
