## Site: Site fields

### `read_site_fields`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/site-fields`

Permission: `read`

Read the site fields: the settings pages (groups with their field definitions), the saved values, updated_at and editable_groups (the groups whose values you may change with your permission). Read this before define_site_fields or update_site_fields and pass its updated_at as expected_updated_at. Site fields are settings pages for the client: a builder defines groups of typed fields once, and the client (an editor) fills in the values without touching pages or design. A group is { id, label, description?, access: "editor" | "admin", fields }. access "editor" (the default) lets anyone who edits content change the values; "admin" only site administrators. Definitions are always site admin. Fields use the content type field model: { name, type, label, required?, help?, placeholder?, default? } with type text, textarea, richtext, boolean (a checkbox, e.g. show_booking), number (min, max), select or multiselect (options), date (2026-11-07), datetime, image, url, email, page_ref, array (a list: fields, item_label, min_items, max_items) or object (a group of fields). Lists and groups nest at most 3 levels. Field names are lowercase_with_underscores and unique across the whole site. Opening hours: an object field with presentation "opening_hours" and exactly this shape (a 7-day week plus dated exceptions such as holidays): {"name":"opening_hours","label":"Opening hours","type":"object","presentation":"opening_hours","fields":[{"name":"days","label":"Week","type":"array","min_items":7,"max_items":7,"item_label":"day","fields":[{"name":"day","label":"Day","type":"select","options":["monday","tuesday","wednesday","thursday","friday","saturday","sunday"]},{"name":"closed","label":"Closed","type":"boolean"},{"name":"opens","label":"Opens","type":"text","placeholder":"09:00"},{"name":"closes","label":"Closes","type":"text","placeholder":"09:00"}]},{"name":"exceptions","label":"Exceptions","type":"array","max_items":60,"item_label":"date","fields":[{"name":"date","label":"Date","type":"date","required":true},{"name":"closed","label":"Closed","type":"boolean"},{"name":"opens","label":"Opens","type":"text"},{"name":"closes","label":"Closes","type":"text"},{"name":"note","label":"Note","type":"text"}]}]} Its value: { days: [{ day: "monday", opens: "09:00", closes: "17:00" }, …, { day: "sunday", closed: true }], exceptions: [{ date: "2026-12-24", closed: true, note: "Christmas Eve" }] }. Using values on the site: `{{site.fields.name}}` (and `{{#each site.fields.list}}…{{/each}}`) in page templates and block text; the `core/site_field` block shows one value with data { field: "name", format } where format is text, date, number, list, opening_hours_today, opening_hours_week, next_opening or open_now; and the `core/show_if` block shows its children only when its condition holds, e.g. { condition: "site.fields.show_booking" } around a booking calendar. Values reach the live site with the next publication, except for a top-level field defined with `live: true` (any type, but no list inside a list; opening hours qualify): its value is also published as a live file when saved, and the `core/site_field` block then shows the newest value without a publication (see list_snippets).

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | query | string | no | Branch id to target. Omit for main. An id that does not name a version of this Site is refused with 404 — it is never answered about main instead. |

### `define_site_fields`

`PUT /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/site-fields`

Permission: `admin`

Replace the site's settings pages (all groups and their field definitions). Needs admin permission on the site. Send every group, including the ones you keep: a group or field left out is removed, and so is its value. Renaming a field is a removal plus an addition, so its value is lost; values that no longer fit a changed field type are dropped too (listed in dropped_values). Example: groups [{ id: "booking", label: "Booking", fields: [{ name: "show_booking", type: "boolean", label: "Show the booking calendar" }, { name: "delivery_days", type: "number", label: "Delivery days right now", min: 0 }] }, { id: "visit", label: "Visit us", fields: [{ name: "visiting_address", type: "textarea", label: "Visiting address", required: true }, &lt;opening hours field&gt; ] }]. Every save keeps the previous document as a revision; invalid definitions return `errors` with the path of each problem. Then fill in values with update_site_fields. Site fields are settings pages for the client: a builder defines groups of typed fields once, and the client (an editor) fills in the values without touching pages or design. A group is { id, label, description?, access: "editor" | "admin", fields }. access "editor" (the default) lets anyone who edits content change the values; "admin" only site administrators. Definitions are always site admin. Fields use the content type field model: { name, type, label, required?, help?, placeholder?, default? } with type text, textarea, richtext, boolean (a checkbox, e.g. show_booking), number (min, max), select or multiselect (options), date (2026-11-07), datetime, image, url, email, page_ref, array (a list: fields, item_label, min_items, max_items) or object (a group of fields). Lists and groups nest at most 3 levels. Field names are lowercase_with_underscores and unique across the whole site. Opening hours: an object field with presentation "opening_hours" and exactly this shape (a 7-day week plus dated exceptions such as holidays): {"name":"opening_hours","label":"Opening hours","type":"object","presentation":"opening_hours","fields":[{"name":"days","label":"Week","type":"array","min_items":7,"max_items":7,"item_label":"day","fields":[{"name":"day","label":"Day","type":"select","options":["monday","tuesday","wednesday","thursday","friday","saturday","sunday"]},{"name":"closed","label":"Closed","type":"boolean"},{"name":"opens","label":"Opens","type":"text","placeholder":"09:00"},{"name":"closes","label":"Closes","type":"text","placeholder":"09:00"}]},{"name":"exceptions","label":"Exceptions","type":"array","max_items":60,"item_label":"date","fields":[{"name":"date","label":"Date","type":"date","required":true},{"name":"closed","label":"Closed","type":"boolean"},{"name":"opens","label":"Opens","type":"text"},{"name":"closes","label":"Closes","type":"text"},{"name":"note","label":"Note","type":"text"}]}]} Its value: { days: [{ day: "monday", opens: "09:00", closes: "17:00" }, …, { day: "sunday", closed: true }], exceptions: [{ date: "2026-12-24", closed: true, note: "Christmas Eve" }] }. Using values on the site: `{{site.fields.name}}` (and `{{#each site.fields.list}}…{{/each}}`) in page templates and block text; the `core/site_field` block shows one value with data { field: "name", format } where format is text, date, number, list, opening_hours_today, opening_hours_week, next_opening or open_now; and the `core/show_if` block shows its children only when its condition holds, e.g. { condition: "site.fields.show_booking" } around a booking calendar. Values reach the live site with the next publication, except for a top-level field defined with `live: true` (any type, but no list inside a list; opening hours qualify): its value is also published as a live file when saved, and the `core/site_field` block then shows the newest value without a publication (see list_snippets).

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `groups` | body | object[] | yes | Every settings page of the site, at most 20 with 200 fields in all. |
| `expected_updated_at` | body | string \| null | no | The updated_at from read_site_fields ("" or null when it was null: nothing saved yet). A save made in between is refused with 409. |
| `version` | query | string | no | Branch id to target. Omit for main. An id that does not name a version of this Site is refused with 404 — it is never answered about main instead. |

### `update_site_fields`

`PATCH /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/site-fields`

Permission: `write`

Change site field values: send only the fields to change, by name; others keep their values, and null removes one. Example: { values: { show_booking: false, delivery_days: 3, opening_hours: { days: [...7 days], exceptions: [{ date: "2026-12-24", closed: true }] } } }. An object or list value is replaced as a whole. Values in groups with access "admin" need admin permission; the rest need write. Saved directly (not a draft), with the previous values kept as a revision; live at the next publication. Invalid values return `errors` with their paths. For the field model and how values show on the site, see read_site_fields.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `values` | body | object | yes | Field name → new value; null removes the value. |
| `expected_updated_at` | body | string \| null | no | The updated_at from read_site_fields ("" or null when it was null: nothing saved yet). A save made in between is refused with 409. |
| `version` | query | string | no | Branch id to target. Omit for main. An id that does not name a version of this Site is refused with 404 — it is never answered about main instead. |

## Site: Snippets

### `list_snippets`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/snippets`

Permission: `read`

List the site's live snippets with their content and updated_at, and `live.base_url`: where their public files are served (null with a reason when the site has no media host, so snippets only change at publication). A live snippet is content outside the build: saving it updates the live site within about a minute, without a publication or a rebuild, so use it for content that changes often (today's lunch, a notice, the current waiting time). Snippets belong to the site (not to a branch), at most 100 per site and 64 KB each. Shape: { id, name, kind, format?, content?, entries?, fallback? }. kind "html": content is HTML, sanitized like page content when saved. kind "text": content is plain text, escaped when shown. kind "dated": entries keyed by date or weekday, and the page shows today's entry in the site's time zone (read_site_settings → time_zone), chosen in the visitor's browser: { kind: "dated", format: "html" | "text", entries: [{ weekday: "monday", content: "…" }, …, { date: "2026-12-24", content: "Closed" }], fallback: "No lunch today" }. A date entry wins over a weekday entry; fallback shows on a day without one. For "today's lunch", write the whole week once (one entry per weekday, plus dated exceptions) instead of saving every day; the file stays unchanged between writes. To show a snippet on a page, place a `core/snippet` block with data { snippet: "&lt;snippet id&gt;" } where it should appear: the page carries the value of the latest publication (for search engines and without script) and the browser then shows the newest. Placing or moving the block is a page edit that needs a publication; changing the snippet afterwards does not. A site field defined with `live: true` (define_site_fields) works the same way for a single value: the `core/site_field` block shows its newest value without publishing. Every save answers `live`: { published: true, url } when the public file was written, or { published: false, reason } when the site has no media host that can serve it (the snippet is still saved and shows at the next publication).

### `read_snippet`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/snippets/{snippet_id}`

Permission: `read`

Read one live snippet, its updated_at (pass it to update_snippet as expected_updated_at) and live_url, the public file the live site reads. For the model, see list_snippets.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `snippet_id` | path | string | yes | The snippet id: lowercase letters, digits, - and _ (for example "lunch"). |

### `update_snippet`

`PUT /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/snippets/{snippet_id}`

Permission: `write`

Create or replace a whole live snippet; it is live within about a minute, without publishing. Send every field you keep: what is left out is removed. Pass the updated_at from read_snippet as expected_updated_at (or "" to create one that must not exist yet); a save made in between is refused with 409. Example (the week's lunch): { snippet_id: "lunch", name: "Lunch", kind: "dated", format: "html", entries: [{ weekday: "monday", content: "&lt;p&gt;Pea soup and pancakes&lt;/p&gt;" }, …], fallback: "&lt;p&gt;No lunch served today&lt;/p&gt;" }. Then show it with a `core/snippet` block { snippet: "lunch" } if no page shows it yet. A live snippet is content outside the build: saving it updates the live site within about a minute, without a publication or a rebuild, so use it for content that changes often (today's lunch, a notice, the current waiting time). Snippets belong to the site (not to a branch), at most 100 per site and 64 KB each. Shape: { id, name, kind, format?, content?, entries?, fallback? }. kind "html": content is HTML, sanitized like page content when saved. kind "text": content is plain text, escaped when shown. kind "dated": entries keyed by date or weekday, and the page shows today's entry in the site's time zone (read_site_settings → time_zone), chosen in the visitor's browser: { kind: "dated", format: "html" | "text", entries: [{ weekday: "monday", content: "…" }, …, { date: "2026-12-24", content: "Closed" }], fallback: "No lunch today" }. A date entry wins over a weekday entry; fallback shows on a day without one. For "today's lunch", write the whole week once (one entry per weekday, plus dated exceptions) instead of saving every day; the file stays unchanged between writes. To show a snippet on a page, place a `core/snippet` block with data { snippet: "&lt;snippet id&gt;" } where it should appear: the page carries the value of the latest publication (for search engines and without script) and the browser then shows the newest. Placing or moving the block is a page edit that needs a publication; changing the snippet afterwards does not. A site field defined with `live: true` (define_site_fields) works the same way for a single value: the `core/site_field` block shows its newest value without publishing. Every save answers `live`: { published: true, url } when the public file was written, or { published: false, reason } when the site has no media host that can serve it (the snippet is still saved and shows at the next publication).

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `snippet_id` | path | string | yes | The snippet id: lowercase letters, digits, - and _ (for example "lunch"). |
| `name` | body | string | yes | The name editors see, for example "Today's lunch". |
| `kind` | body | "html" \| "text" \| "dated" | yes |  |
| `format` | body | "html" \| "text" | no | dated snippets: whether entries are HTML (default) or plain text. |
| `content` | body | string | no | html and text snippets: the content. |
| `entries` | body | object[] | no | dated snippets: entries by weekday or date, at most 400. |
| `fallback` | body | string | no | dated snippets: shown on a day without an entry. |
| `expected_updated_at` | body | string \| null | no | The updated_at you read; "" or null for a new snippet. |

### `delete_snippet`

`DELETE /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/snippets/{snippet_id}`

Permission: `write`

Delete a live snippet and its public file. A `core/snippet` block that still shows it keeps the value of the latest publication until the page is published again; remove the block too. Pass expected_updated_at to refuse deleting a snippet changed since you read it.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `snippet_id` | path | string | yes | The snippet id: lowercase letters, digits, - and _ (for example "lunch"). |
| `expected_updated_at` | query | string | no | The updated_at you read. |

## Site: Styles

### `list_styles`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/styles`

Permission: `read`

List the site's named style library: element roles (body, h1–h6, link) that style every matching element, and the styles blocks select with `style_id`. Also returns missing_standard_roles, contrast/library problems and readability warnings (both APCA Lc and WCAG 2 ratio). READ THIS BEFORE STYLING ANY PAGE: reuse an existing style for a recurring look (eyebrows, leads, card titles, buttons, section spacing) instead of per-block values, raw HTML classes or page CSS.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | query | string | no | Branch id to target. Omit for main. An id that does not name a version of this Site is refused with 404 — it is never answered about main instead. |

### `create_style`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/styles`

Permission: `write`

Create a named style. Do this whenever a look could recur — an eyebrow, a lead paragraph, a card title, a quote, a button variant, a section rhythm — then apply it with the block's `style_id` field. Only a clearly unique one-off may use block settings instead. Set values for phones in `base` and grow them in `at.tablet`/`at.desktop`. Text contrast against its background is measured with APCA by use, size and weight (body text Lc 75; secondary/small text Lc 60; headings, eyebrows and buttons Lc 60 from 16px at weight 600+, Lc 45 from 24px bold or 36px; smaller or lighter non-body text Lc 75) and with the WCAG 2 ratio. Text that fails both is refused; text below its APCA level that meets WCAG 2 AA (4.5:1, 3:1 for ≥24px or bold ≥18.7px) is saved and returned in `warnings`. Never light grey on white. To restyle a sub-element of a block (rich-heading links, a hero's buttons or image), list it in `parts` (site-wide) or choose the style in that block's `data.part_styles`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | body | string | yes | Stable slug; the CSS class becomes s-&lt;id&gt;. Cannot change later. |
| `name` | body | string | yes | Author-facing name, in the site's language, e.g. "Överrubrik" or "Hero title". |
| `role` | body | "body" \| "h1" \| "h2" \| "h3" \| "h4" \| "h5" \| "h6" \| "link" \| "lead" \| "eyebrow" \| "small" \| "quote" \| "button" \| "button_secondary" \| "section" | no | Standard role. body/h1–h6/link style every matching element on the site; the others mark the standard style for that purpose. One style per role. |
| `targets` | body | "text" \| "heading" \| "list" \| "button" \| "container" \| "link" \| "image"[] | no | Kinds of element that can select this style: through a block's style_id (text = core/prose, heading = core/heading and core/rich_heading, list, button, container = core/section and core/container) and through a block part with that target (link and image exist for parts, e.g. core/rich_heading.link, core/hero.media). |
| `description` | body | string | no | When to use it; shown to editors and agents. |
| `base` | body | object | no | Style properties. Mobile-first: `base` applies everywhere, `at.<breakpoint>` from that width up. |
| `at` | body | object | no | Overrides from each site breakpoint upward (tablet, laptop, desktop, wide). |
| `hover` | body | object | no |  |
| `visited` | body | object | no | Link role only: the colour of visited links (:visited). Hover still wins on a visited link. |
| `css` | body | string | no | Advanced CSS scoped to the style: bare declarations, or rules where `&` is the style selector (e.g. "&amp;::before { content: '—' }"). Prefer structured properties. |
| `parts` | body | string[] | no | Block parts this style applies to SITE-WIDE, on every instance, as "&lt;block type&gt;.&lt;part&gt;" (e.g. "core/rich_heading.link", "core/hero.primary_button"); read_block_type lists a block's `parts` with their targets. The style's targets must include each part's target; a part takes one site-wide style; not for element roles (body, h1–h6, link). Unknown parts are refused with the closest names. Precedence, lowest first: the block's own CSS and fields; this site-wide part style, replaced on one block by its `data.part_styles` choice; a style class on the element itself (a heading's eyebrow_style_id, a button's style_id). |
| `version` | query | string | no | Branch id to target. Omit for main. An id that does not name a version of this Site is refused with 404 — it is never answered about main instead. |

### `update_style`

`PATCH /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/styles/{style_id}`

Permission: `write`

Update a style. `base`, `hover`, `visited` and each breakpoint in `at` merge property by property (pass null to remove one); name, targets, description, css and parts replace (parts: [] removes the style from every part). Every page using the style changes at once — tell the user which pages that affects when it matters.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `style_id` | path | string | yes |  |
| `name` | body | string | no | Author-facing name, in the site's language, e.g. "Överrubrik" or "Hero title". |
| `role` | body | "body" \| "h1" \| "h2" \| "h3" \| "h4" \| "h5" \| "h6" \| "link" \| "lead" \| "eyebrow" \| "small" \| "quote" \| "button" \| "button_secondary" \| "section" | no | Standard role. body/h1–h6/link style every matching element on the site; the others mark the standard style for that purpose. One style per role. |
| `targets` | body | "text" \| "heading" \| "list" \| "button" \| "container" \| "link" \| "image"[] | no | Kinds of element that can select this style: through a block's style_id (text = core/prose, heading = core/heading and core/rich_heading, list, button, container = core/section and core/container) and through a block part with that target (link and image exist for parts, e.g. core/rich_heading.link, core/hero.media). |
| `description` | body | string | no | When to use it; shown to editors and agents. |
| `base` | body | object | no | Property patch for base; null removes a property. |
| `at` | body | object | no | Per-breakpoint property patches; null removes a breakpoint or property. |
| `hover` | body | object | no |  |
| `visited` | body | object | no |  |
| `css` | body | string | no |  |
| `parts` | body | string[] | no | Block parts this style applies to SITE-WIDE, on every instance, as "&lt;block type&gt;.&lt;part&gt;" (e.g. "core/rich_heading.link", "core/hero.primary_button"); read_block_type lists a block's `parts` with their targets. The style's targets must include each part's target; a part takes one site-wide style; not for element roles (body, h1–h6, link). Unknown parts are refused with the closest names. Precedence, lowest first: the block's own CSS and fields; this site-wide part style, replaced on one block by its `data.part_styles` choice; a style class on the element itself (a heading's eyebrow_style_id, a button's style_id). |
| `version` | query | string | no | Branch id to target. Omit for main. An id that does not name a version of this Site is refused with 404 — it is never answered about main instead. |

### `delete_style`

`DELETE /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/styles/{style_id}`

Permission: `write`

Delete a style. Blocks that still reference it fall back to their default look; reassign them first.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `style_id` | path | string | yes |  |
| `version` | query | string | no | Branch id to target. Omit for main. An id that does not name a version of this Site is refused with 404 — it is never answered about main instead. |

### `apply_standard_styles`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/styles/standard`

Permission: `write`

Add the standard styles the site is missing (body, H1–H6, link, lead, eyebrow, small text, quote, primary/secondary button, section), with considered sizes and spacing for phones, tablets and desktops. The natural first step when building a new site, before pages: then adjust them to the brand (fonts, colours, scale) with update_style. New sites already have them. overwrite:true resets the standard roles to the defaults and changes the site's look — ask first. A standard style whose palette colour is unreadable on the background is added with the body text colour instead; `adjusted` lists those and `warnings` says what changed, with the measures — tell the user.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `overwrite` | body | boolean | no |  |
| `version` | query | string | no | Branch id to target. Omit for main. An id that does not name a version of this Site is refused with 404 — it is never answered about main instead. |

## Site: Versions

### `list_versions`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/versions`

Permission: `read`

List versions (main + branches).

### `create_branch`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/versions`

Permission: `admin`

Create a copy-on-write branch from main (or the version passed in `base`) — the RECOMMENDED first step for any larger or experimental change (redesigns, multi-page edits, trying a new design direction). Work lands on the branch, never on the live main version, until you merge_branch it. New branches default to robots_blocked:true (a half-finished design can't be indexed) and get their own stable deploy address for stakeholder review: after the branch's first trigger_deploy, read it from deploy_url in list_versions or read_version (the publishing setup decides the host: under a Hosting Group it is a v-… host under that group's site address base, otherwise the address the host reported; never construct it yourself). Pass the returned id as ?version= on every subsequent read/write. When in doubt, branch — it's cheap and keeps the live site safe. The tr-redesign-branch skill (read_skill) walks the full flow. Admin permission on the site is required, as in the portal.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | body | string | yes |  |
| `base` | body | string | no | Source version id; defaults to main. |

### `read_version`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/versions/{version_id}`

Permission: `read`

Read one version's metadata.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version_id` | path | string | yes |  |

### `delete_branch`

`DELETE /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/versions/{version_id}`

Permission: `admin`

Discard a branch with its overrides, tombstones and revision history (main cannot be deleted). Admin permission required.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version_id` | path | string | yes |  |

### `diff_version`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/versions/{version_id}/diff`

Permission: `read`

Read-only: what a branch changes relative to main, per collection (pages, partials, redirects, contentTypes, pageTemplates, blockTypes): ids it adds, modifies and deletes, plus whether it overrides site settings and totalChanges. This is exactly what merge_branch would land on main and what reset_version would discard. Use it to summarise a branch for review before asking for merge approval.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version_id` | path | string | yes | Branch id (main has nothing to diff). |

### `reset_version`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/versions/{version_id}/reset`

Permission: `admin`

Discard EVERY change on a branch (all overrides and deletions), so it reads straight through to main again. The branch itself, its deploy address and its revision history are kept. Destructive for the branch's work: run diff_version first and get explicit user approval. Returns { cleared } — the diff that was discarded. Admin permission required. Main cannot be reset.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version_id` | path | string | yes |  |

### `merge_branch`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/versions/{version_id}/merge`

Permission: `admin`

Promote a branch's overrides + tombstones onto main (diff_version shows exactly what will land). The branch is left in place so you can keep iterating; delete_branch removes it when you're done. Admin permission required.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version_id` | path | string | yes |  |

## Site: Workflows

### `list_workflows`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/workflows`

Permission: `read`

List the workflow types this Site can run (label, description, steps, required_permission) and its most recent runs with status. Read only. Migration, site planning and URL parity pause for review; check get_workflow for paused_for_review. A run left running after a service restart is reported failed with failure_code workflow_interrupted. Site planning, content generation, content improvement and schema markup need the Organization's AI key for this Site (see start_workflow).

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | query | integer | no |  |

### `start_workflow`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/workflows`

Permission: `write`

Start a server-side workflow on this Site; it runs in the background and returns workflow_id. Poll get_workflow. Config per type (same fields as the portal form): migration { wp_url, helper_api_key? } (needs verified organization import storage); site_planning { business_description }; content_generation { topic, tone?, audience? }; content_improvement { limit? }; url_parity { target_origin?, source_origin?, check_source?, statuses? }; rebuild_deploy { environment: staging | production, confirm_live_domains? } (queues a publication like trigger_deploy; its result carries job_id for get_deploy_status. Production on a cut-over site publishes to its live domain and needs confirm_live_domains: true after owner approval); seo_audit, link_check, performance_audit and schema_markup take none. Needs write permission; rebuild_deploy publishes and needs admin. Workflows that change content write to the given version (default main) — get the user's agreement first. AI workflows — site_planning, content_generation, content_improvement and schema_markup — call the model with the Organization's own AI key and need AI access for this Site; without it the run fails with failure_code "ai_not_enabled" (failure_reason: the AI assistant is not enabled for this site). Do not retry or work around it: you are an AI agent, so do the same work yourself and tell the user you did — site_planning: tr-new-site (propose the page structure, get approval, then build); content_generation: tr-content-write (draft page); content_improvement: tr-content-write on the weakest published pages (thin text, missing seo_title/seo_description, stale), as unsaved drafts for review; schema_markup: tr-seo step 5 (add_faq_schema, add_recipe_schema, add_event_schema or json_ld). seo_audit still runs without AI and returns its issue list unprioritized. Enabling the portal AI is the Organization owner's or admin's choice, never a prerequisite for you.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | body | "migration" \| "site_planning" \| "seo_audit" \| "content_improvement" \| "link_check" \| "performance_audit" \| "content_generation" \| "schema_markup" \| "url_parity" \| "rebuild_deploy" | yes |  |
| `config` | body | object | no |  |
| `version` | query | string | no | Branch id to target. Omit for main. An id that does not name a version of this Site is refused with 404 — it is never answered about main instead. |

### `get_workflow`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/workflows/{workflow_id}`

Permission: `read`

Read one workflow run: status (pending | running | paused_for_review | completed | failed | cancelled), current step, progress, log, review_message/review_data when paused, results, failure_reason and failure_code (newer Core; older Core reports failure_reason only). Credential config is masked. failure_code "ai_not_enabled" (or a failure_reason saying the AI assistant is not enabled for this site) means the Site has no portal AI access: do the work yourself with the recipe named in start_workflow instead of retrying. failure_code "workflow_interrupted" means the run stopped making progress (no heartbeat for over 10 minutes, usually because the service restarted) and will not continue: tell the user, then start_workflow again; work saved before it stopped stays saved. A run that is still running keeps a recent heartbeat_at, however slowly it progresses.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workflow_id` | path | string | yes |  |

### `approve_workflow`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/workflows/{workflow_id}/approve`

Permission: `write`

Approve the review gate of a run that is paused_for_review; it resumes from the next step in the background. Show the user review_message and review_data from get_workflow and get their approval first — approval is theirs to give, not the tool's. Write permission; any other status returns 409.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workflow_id` | path | string | yes |  |

### `cancel_workflow`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/workflows/{workflow_id}/cancel`

Permission: `write`

Cancel a run that is pending, running or paused_for_review; it is recorded as status cancelled and continues no further (a step already in flight may finish its current work, but nothing more is recorded; changes it already saved stay). Use it when the user wants to stop a run or start over. Needs the permission that starting the type needs (write; admin for rebuild_deploy). A finished run (completed, failed, cancelled) returns 409. Returns the cancelled run.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workflow_id` | path | string | yes |  |

## Site: Working copy

### `read_working_copy`

`GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/working-copy/page/{id}`

Permission: `read`

Templates save immediately and do not use this tool. Use target: {kind: page|partial, id: ...}, not page_id. Read a doc's unsaved draft (working copy) as a raw field diff — { working_copy: null } means everything is saved. read_page/get_page_blocks already return the draft VIEW; use this when you need to know exactly WHICH fields are unsaved, e.g. before discarding (the draft may hold the user's in-progress editor work, not just yours).

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `target` | query | object | yes | Which doc's draft: page {id} or partial {id}. Templates have no drafts (their writes apply directly). |
| `version` | query | string | no | Branch id to target. Omit for main. An id that does not name a version of this Site is refused with 404 — it is never answered about main instead. |

### `commit_working_copy`

`POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/working-copy/page/{id}`

Permission: `write`

SAVE a doc's unsaved draft: promote it onto the saved doc through the canonical write path (revision snapshot, SEO transform, redirect hygiene) and delete the draft. Identical to the Save button in the portal editor. Returns { committed, seo_warnings, auto_redirects, retired_redirects }. Never changes publish status. Deploys only ship saved content, so commit before trigger_deploy. Equivalent shortcut: save:true on the write tools.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `target` | body | object | yes | Which doc's draft: page {id} or partial {id}. Templates have no drafts (their writes apply directly). |
| `override_reason` | body | string | no | Why a value the listed business set itself (through its edit link) is being replaced. Required only for those values, as in the portal; the write otherwise returns 409 naming the field. |
| `version` | query | string | no | Branch id to target. Omit for main. An id that does not name a version of this Site is refused with 404 — it is never answered about main instead. |

### `discard_working_copy`

`DELETE /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/working-copy/page/{id}`

Permission: `write`

Throw away a doc's unsaved draft — the saved doc is untouched. Use when the user rejects the previewed change. CAUTION: the draft is shared with the human editor; read_working_copy first if you're not sure whose edits are in it.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `target` | query | object | yes | Which doc's draft: page {id} or partial {id}. Templates have no drafts (their writes apply directly). |
| `version` | query | string | no | Branch id to target. Omit for main. An id that does not name a version of this Site is refused with 404 — it is never answered about main instead. |

## Sites

### `list_sites`

`GET /api/v1/sites`

Permission: `read`

List accessible Sites without changing them. Use the returned IDs for site_id or your workspace binding. Results are paginated locally.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `offset` | query | integer | no |  |
| `limit` | query | integer | no |  |

### `create_site`

`POST /api/v1/sites`

Permission: `write`

Create + bootstrap a NEW site in your org. Seeds default settings, a published Home page, and a published header/footer that link only to it, so it renders and can be published immediately. Requires an ORG-scoped key (a site-scoped key is bound to one existing site and can't mint new ones; you'll get a 403). Accepts exactly `name`, optional `id`, `domain` and `language`; any other field is refused. Without `id` the site id is the kebab-case `name` (with a random suffix when taken); with `id` that exact id is used, or 409 site_id_taken. `language` is the site's BCP 47 content language (e.g. "nl-BE"; default "en"), saved at creation so &lt;html lang&gt; is right from the first build. Pass `domain` to kick off the "point your DNS" flow (never written as a live domain). Returns the new site's id, language + urls — use that id as `site_id`/`TYPEROLL_SITE_ID` for follow-up calls. After creating, run list_skills → read_skill tr-new-site to bootstrap the design.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | body | string | yes | Display name. Slugified into the site id unless `id` is given. |
| `id` | body | string | no | Optional site id: 3-48 lowercase letters, digits and "-" (e.g. "acme-studio"). Used exactly; 409 site_id_taken when the organization has it. Default: the kebab-case name. |
| `language` | body | string | no | Optional site content language as a BCP 47 tag (e.g. "en", "sv", "nl-BE"). Default "en". Drives &lt;html lang&gt;; change it later with update_site_settings. |
| `domain` | body | string | no | Optional real hostname e.g. "example.com". Starts DNS setup; not set live until DNS verifies. |

### `create_site_and_migrate`

`POST /api/v1/sites/create-and-migrate`

Permission: `write`

Create a new Site in the Organization and start a WordPress migration into it, like "Migrate from WordPress" on the portal's New site page. Requires an organization API key and verified organization import storage (409 import_storage_required otherwise — nothing is created). Returns site and workflow ids; poll get_workflow with that site_id. Run get_migration_readiness on the new Site if you need the preflight first. Optional `id` and `language` work as in create_site; any other field is refused.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | body | string | yes | Site display name; slugified into the Site id unless `id` is given. |
| `id` | body | string | no | Optional site id: 3-48 lowercase letters, digits and "-" (e.g. "acme-studio"). Used exactly; 409 site_id_taken when the organization has it. Default: the kebab-case name. |
| `language` | body | string | no | Optional site content language as a BCP 47 tag (e.g. "en", "sv", "nl-BE"). Default "en". Drives &lt;html lang&gt;; change it later with update_site_settings. |
| `wp_url` | body | string | yes | Public WordPress address, e.g. https://oldsite.example. |
| `helper_api_key` | body | string | no | Typeroll Helper plugin key from the WordPress admin, if installed. Stored for the run and never returned. |

### `create_site_and_plan`

`POST /api/v1/sites/create-and-plan`

Permission: `write`

Create a new Site in the Organization and start AI site planning from a business description, like "Plan a new site with AI" on the New site page. Requires an organization API key. Needs the Organization's own AI key with site access "all" (read_organization_ai_settings); otherwise it answers 403 ai_not_enabled and creates nothing — then create_site a blank Site and plan it yourself with tr-new-site (propose the pages, get the user's approval, build), and say that you did; enabling the portal AI is the owner's or admin's choice, not a prerequisite. The plan pauses for review: read it with get_workflow and approve_workflow only after the user agrees. Optional `id` and `language` work as in create_site; any other field is refused.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | body | string | yes | Site display name; slugified into the Site id unless `id` is given. |
| `id` | body | string | no | Optional site id: 3-48 lowercase letters, digits and "-" (e.g. "acme-studio"). Used exactly; 409 site_id_taken when the organization has it. Default: the kebab-case name. |
| `language` | body | string | no | Optional site content language as a BCP 47 tag (e.g. "en", "sv", "nl-BE"). Default "en". Drives &lt;html lang&gt;; change it later with update_site_settings. |
| `business_description` | body | string | yes | What the business does, for whom, and what sets it apart. |
